title: Jobs-per-Megawatt Factory Recruiting for Public Power
angle: Pairing 2: Reshoring, tariffs & automation x Government / defense / municipal
one_liner: Represent municipal electric utilities in recruiting manufacturers by packaging spare feeder capacity, in-hand transformers and industrial rates into a 'jobs per megawatt' pitch that data centers cannot match.
customer: Municipal and public-power utilities and city economic-development agencies (retainer of roughly $3-6k a month). Manufacturers pay a success fee later.
problem: Data centers are absorbing grid capacity, and transformer and switchgear prices are up 89-96% since 2019. Factory construction is down 22-32% from peak while nondefense capital-goods orders hit a record $85.9B, so reshoring is happening as retrofits that need power upgrades, not as new shells. Interconnection at investor-owned utilities takes years, and site selectors rarely look at small public utilities.
solution: A 'Load-Readiness Dossier' per feeder or substation: available megawatts, transformer status and lead times, industrial rate schedules, demand-charge modeling and permitting path. Match it to manufacturers with announced expansions (tariff-motivated onshoring, USMCA re-routers, foundries and magnet or metal processors) and to site selectors. Add a shared transformer reserve pool for small municipal utilities and help negotiate long-term service commitments.
why_now: Data-center demand collided with the reshoring wave in 2026. Section 232 tiers reward US-melted metals and full-value duties are pushing firms to add domestic capacity, and the machinery tier's 15% relief runs through 2027. Utilities are being asked to make loads decisions faster than most can handle.
revenue_model: $3-6k a month retainer per utility, a success fee per megawatt or per signed customer (paid by the manufacturer or shared), and optional financing of pre-bought transformer inventory.
non_obvious_insight: A public utility's incentives are the reverse of an investor-owned utility's. A 5 MW machining plant with hundreds of jobs beats a 100 MW data center with a few dozen jobs for a city council and for spreading fixed costs, yet no one markets to these utilities. Transformer-in-hand is the strongest closing argument.
first_30_days: Select 10 public-power utilities in manufacturing states (Ohio, Indiana, Tennessee, Texas, the Carolinas) and build dossiers from public tariffs, EIA data and integrated resource plans. Pitch 3 economic-development agencies and sign two paid pilot retainers.

title: Tariff Forward Curve for Section 232 Lists
one_liner: A probability feed for which HTS codes join the next Section 232 lists, with parametric hedges to follow.
customer: CFOs and sourcing heads at importers with metal-heavy lines and $20M-$1B revenue, and trade counsel. Insurers and MGAs later.
problem: Firms treat tariffs as unpredictable, so they pre-buy a year of inventory or freeze decisions. But Section 232 additions run through a public administrative pipeline of industry petitions and comment periods (the latest request for comments on 2026-08-06). Other actions carry visible dates: polysilicon at 15% with minimum import prices from 2026-12-04, and a robotics and machinery investigation still pending. Nobody publishes odds.
solution: Model each HTS-10's probability and timing of inclusion or rate change using past inclusion rounds (petitioner identity, domestic producer concentration, import share, comment volume). Update as dockets move. Deliver a dashboard, API and Slack alerts. Phase 2 is a parametric cover with an MGA or event-contract venue that pays if a heading's rate rises by a set amount within 12 months, priced off the curve.
why_now: With IEEPA gone, Section 232 is the main channel. The inclusion process is open and docketed, LLMs can read comments at scale, and event-contract and parametric markets have grown.
revenue_model: $1.5-5k a month subscription. Later, commission or spread on hedges.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders call tariffs political noise, but 232 additions follow petitioners who show up months earlier. Even 65% accuracy is worth far more than the fee to a firm deciding whether to pre-buy. Tracking current rates is crowded, but forecasting future inclusion is not.
first_30_days: Scrape BIS inclusion dockets and Federal Register notices. Hand-label the last two rounds. Publish a free weekly 'next 232 list watch' newsletter. Sign five paid pilots from importers with more than $500k of metal-derivative exposure.

title: 48-Hour Takedown Desk for Small Platforms
one_liner: A hosted notice-and-removal service that lets small user-content platforms meet the TAKE IT DOWN Act's 48-hour clock while filtering out weaponized false claims.
customer: Small and mid-size platforms hosting user content: niche forums, community and chat servers, creator and fan-content sites, marketplaces with seller photos, dating apps, and indie AI image and video generators. They pay $99-$2,000/month.
problem: Since 19 May 2026, covered platforms must run a removal process and take down non-consensual intimate imagery, including deepfakes and known identical copies, within 48 hours of a valid request. The FTC is enforcing, has sent warning letters to a dozen sites of varying sizes and can seek penalties above $50k per violation. Small teams cannot staff weekends or nights. The statute has no counter-notice or penalty for false claims, so bad-faith takedown floods by rivals or harassers are a real censorship tool.
solution: A drop-in intake page, API and email alias. Requesters are identity-verified and their signed statement is captured. Trained reviewers work 24/7 with a 4-hour internal target. Hash and perceptual matching (including StopNCII) finds copies across the customer's site. The desk executes removals, logs evidence and produces a monthly FTC-ready compliance report. A shared claimant-reputation graph flags serial or coordinated false claimants across customers, with configurable reinstatement policies.
why_now: Enforcement is live and visibly reaching small sites. AI image generators multiply NCII volume. Small platforms that could ignore trust and safety until now have a hard federal clock.
revenue_model: Subscription tiered by monthly active users and case volume, plus a per-case fee above quota. Enterprise plans for AI image and video generators, and an add-on for FTC inquiry support.
non_obvious_insight: Detection is not the scarce resource, since StopNCII and hashing already exist. The scarce resources are accountable human judgment on a 48-hour clock and cross-platform intelligence on abusive claimants, which only a shared vendor can see. The law's missing abuse safeguard is the product.
first_30_days: Build intake and workflow on Retool or Airtable with 6 ex-trust-and-safety reviewers across two time zones. Contact 100 small platforms found via FTC warning-letter coverage and forum and community host lists, offering a 30-day free pilot. Publish a free compliance checklist for lead capture, then charge $199/month from the second month.

title: Lifetime Income Leases for Retiring Farmers' Water
angle: Pairing 1: Aging/eldercare/silver economy x Water scarcity/infrastructure
one_liner: A 'water pension' that turns a retiring farm couple's senior Colorado River water right into guaranteed, inheritable lifetime income via a long-term forbearance lease, satellite-verified and sold as verified acre-feet to cities and corporates.
customer: Buyers are municipal water agencies, Lower Basin cities, corporate water-stewardship funds (such as the Water Resilience Coalition Amazon put $20M into) and conservation programs. Sellers are farm owners 62+ without farming heirs. Money moves as multi-year lease payments, and the firm keeps 8-12%.
problem: About 70% of the Colorado River goes to agriculture, and the 2027-2036 framework (Record of Decision, Aug 2026) forces the next cuts onto farms, with Powell and Mead near 36% full. 'Buy-and-dry' sales are politically toxic. Lump-sum sales trigger capital gains and do not fund a long retirement, and urban heirs inherit water rights they cannot operate. Buyers want verified acre-feet, but no settlement layer exists.
solution: A 15-30-year forbearance (rotational fallowing or deficit irrigation) on a slice of the right. Payments are indexed and pass to the surviving spouse, then to a trust. An estate-plan wrapper (trust holds the right with the lease attached, plus CPA and water-attorney advice on tax basis and long-term-care planning) makes it a retirement product. Consumptive-use reduction is verified by satellite evapotranspiration data and paid quarterly. Title never leaves the family, which defuses buy-and-dry politics for the buyer.
why_now: The 10-year framework was finalized in Aug 2026 and storage is the lowest since 1963. Corporate money is arriving ($32M raised toward a $100M goal) with no settlement layer. US drought coverage is 49.6%. A generation of irrigators is reaching retirement with no successors.
revenue_model: 8-12% of lease flows, a buyer-paid verification subscription per acre-foot, and a $3-5k planning fee per family.
non_obvious_insight: Older water-right owners often refuse to sell at any price but will accept certainty of income for life while keeping title. Water brokers are paid on transfers, not on retirements, so nobody sells water as a pension asset. The retirement-income framing is what makes the supply available.
first_30_days: Pick one district (Palo Verde Valley CA, Yuma AZ or Grand Valley CO). Run three kitchen-table workshops with an ag lender, a CPA and a water attorney to enroll about 10 couples. Get a non-binding letter of intent from one buyer for 500-2,000 acre-feet. Check the state rules on temporary transfers first.

title: Actual-Play Sessions Turned Into Animated Episodes
one_liner: A pipeline that turns a tabletop RPG stream's audio and character art into a condensed animated episode using the cast's own voices, with human review.
customer: Actual-play shows and TTRPG creators with 3k-50k Patreon patrons, and TTRPG publishers wanting marketing series.
problem: Fans want animated adaptations, but animation costs millions. Creators have hundreds of hours of audio and no way to give patrons a visual product.
solution: Ingest the session audio and each creator's character art bible. An LLM editor condenses a 4-hour session into a 12-20 minute script. Video generation uses per-character references trained only on the creator's own art, with consenting voices and lip-sync, and a producer reviews each cut. Output includes premium-tier episodes and short clips for growth.
why_now: Video models now generate consistent characters with synced audio, and creators can use their own art and voices with disclosure, which sidesteps most of the AI-slop backlash.
revenue_model: $1.5-5k per episode or 20-30% of new patron revenue for 12 months, plus a licensing fee for publishers.
non_obvious_insight: The output is not cinema but the recap format, the 'previously on' fans share, and the same pipeline produces shorts that grow the channel. Consent and disclosure are the differentiators.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 mid-size actual-play creators. Produce one 90-second pilot for each from public sessions, and refine. Sell 3 paid episodes at $1.5k.

title: Distressed Cargo Rescue Desk for Bankrupt Importers
one_liner: A broker-run desk that takes orphaned containers from failed importers, clears the four-way legal tangle in days, and delivers the goods to off-price buyers at deep discounts.
customer: Off-price retailers, closeout buyers and liquidators who cannot currently buy orphaned cargo because they are not the consignee. Carriers and CFS operators, who want the boxes gone, and trustees, who want recovery, are the supply side. The buyer pays a handling fee or a spread.
problem: When a small importer fails mid-shipment, the goods sit on the water or on a terminal with no ISF, no entry, no bond and a demurrage and storage clock running. The bills of lading are in a dead company's name. Carriers and warehouses will not release cargo to strangers. Buyers would pay well for the goods but cannot make entry. Unentered cargo can be sent to a General Order warehouse after about 15 days and is subject to public sale after roughly six months, so value bleeds out. Many boxes are eventually abandoned, auctioned for pennies or destroyed. The 2025-26 tariff whiplash left a long tail of failed importers, and Long Beach's record volumes keep yard space and free time expensive.
solution: Run a cargo rescue desk with five steps. (1) Source: call carriers' demurrage collection desks, CFS warehouses in Carson and Long Beach, and bankruptcy trustees to find orphaned cargo. (2) Screen: triage compliance risk (CPSC certification, FDA, FCC, UFLPA and IPR issues) and refuse any box that cannot be legally sold. (3) Title: obtain the trustee's or owner's transfer of cargo rights and a negotiated carrier release, trading the removal of the box for a waiver or reduction of demurrage. (4) Entry: the purchaser, as an actual purchaser with the right to make entry, becomes importer of record on a single-transaction bond, with a licensed broker filing the entry. (5) Deliver to the buyer's warehouse. Where the invoices are non-compliant, a dispute of the demurrage under the FMC's billing rules adds leverage.
why_now: Small-brand failures peaked through the 2025 tariff shock and its aftershocks. The IEEPA reversal of Feb 2026 has estates now holding refund cash but still holding stranded physical goods. Off-price retail demand for cheap inventory is high. Single-transaction customs bonds mean a new team does not need a continuous bond or big capital to start.
revenue_model: 10-15% handling and sourcing fee on landed cost from the buyer, or a resale spread on consignment goods. Add trustee-side success fees where the desk increases estate recovery. Duties and fees are pre-funded by the buyer, so the desk avoids inventory risk in the early phase.
non_obvious_insight: A container of orphaned goods is worth its inventory value minus the clock. The party that can solve four separate systems (bill-of-lading rights, the carrier lien and demurrage, customs entry and IOR, and compliance screening) in days captures the discount. VCs treat liquidation as a marketplace problem. It is a legal-plumbing problem, and only a customs broker knows how the entry, bond and purchaser-as-IOR pieces fit together.
first_30_days: Line up a partner bond agent for single-transaction bonds and one buyer network of 5-10 off-price and closeout buyers. Call demurrage collections and terminal-side contacts at 10 carriers and 10 CFS warehouses with a simple offer: we clear abandoned cargo if you waive charges. Ask two bankruptcy trustees whether any estate holds cargo. Close the first 2-3 rescues in the 30-60 day window with fully buyer-funded duties.

title: Compute Boilers: Servers That Heat Buildings
one_liner: Install liquid-cooled inference servers in the boiler rooms of hotels, dorms, pools and laundries, sell the compute, and give the building cheap hot water.
customer: Hotels, university housing, municipal pools and YMCAs, multifamily buildings with central hot water, and laundries. They get cheaper heat. Inference providers buy the compute.
problem: Large AI sites wait years in interconnection queues, yet buildings already have continuous thermal loads, existing 3-phase service and unused headroom. Sub-MW loads avoid large-load studies. Owners face pressure to electrify hot water and building-emissions fines such as NYC's Local Law 97.
solution: Sealed 30-100 kW direct-to-chip liquid-cooled modules plumbed into building hot-water loops that capture most of the heat. The company owns and operates the hardware and sells GPU-hours to inference customers through a neocloud partner. The host gets heat at a discount to its gas or electric cost. First product: 20-40 kW pilots at about 10 hotels and pools in one metro.
why_now: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling is now standard, AI demand exceeds grid supply, small-model inference fits ordinary fiber, and UK pool and hot-water-cylinder server projects prove the model.
revenue_model: Compute revenue share, heat sold to hosts at 50-70% of their current fuel cost, and GPU-lender financing of the hardware.
non_obvious_insight: The grid is not short of electrons. It is short of interconnection at big sites. Sub-MW building sites already have service and a thermal sink, and heat reuse lowers hosting cost below any standalone data center, so the queue is bypassed.
first_30_days: Sign LOIs with five hospitality or pool operators in a state with cheap power and good fiber. Run heat-load audits. Spec a module with a liquid-cooling OEM. Get a GPU-lender term sheet. Deploy a 10 kW test unit at one site.

title: Friday Programs for Four-Day School Districts
one_liner: A turnkey 'fifth-day' care and enrichment operator that runs in existing school buildings for districts on four-day weeks, funded by parent fees and vouchers.
customer: Rural and small-town districts on four-day weeks (hundreds of districts across 20+ states, from memory) and their working parents. Also 21st CCLC and state after-school grant programs.
problem: Districts adopted four-day weeks to cut costs and recruit teachers. The off day leaves working parents with no care in places where licensed slots are already scarce, so kids stay alone, with grandparents or parents leave jobs. Each district improvises its own Friday program.
solution: An operating kit: a staffing pool (education majors and retired teachers), background-check pipeline, daily curriculum, parent sign-up and payment, subsidy-voucher billing, insurance and transport. The district provides the building. We run the first sites ourselves, then license the kit for a management fee.
why_now: ESSER money ended, so more districts are trimming days (from memory). Childcare prices are up 29% since 2020 and rural supply is thin. CCDF rules moving to enrollment-based payment help small operators get paid reliably.
revenue_model: Parent fee of $35-50 per child per day, with a 15% management fee or per-site licence when franchised to local operators. Voucher billing adds funded slots.
non_obvious_insight: This desert is a day-of-week desert created by a policy choice, and the most expensive input (the building) is already paid for by taxpayers. That makes the unit economics better than standard childcare.
first_30_days: Call 20 four-day-week districts in Missouri, Oklahoma and Colorado. Run one paid pilot Friday with 15-25 kids at $40 a day. Recruit staff from the nearest college's education program. Track true margin per child-day and use the data to sell the second district.

title: 30-Day Capacity-Window Plan After Early Alzheimer's Diagnosis
one_liner: A productized sprint that uses the legally competent window after an early blood-test diagnosis to lock down legal, financial, safety and care plans.
customer: Newly diagnosed patients and their spouses or adult children, reached through memory clinics, neurology and primary-care practices, blood-test labs and elder-law firms. Employers with caregiver benefits are a secondary buyer.
problem: Blood tests cleared in 2025 mean many people learn they're on the path to dementia while still competent, with a 3-7 year window to sign POAs, choose agents, set financial guardrails, plan driving and firearm safety, decide on Leqembi and record wishes. After capacity is lost, it becomes a court fight. CMS GUIDE closed enrollment after one 2024 window, so nobody owns the first 30 days.
solution: A fixed-fee, nurse-navigator-led sprint: a capacity-timed legal package via partner attorneys (POAs, directives, HIPAA releases, updated will or trust), financial guardrails (bill-pay automation, bank trusted-contact, scam locks), a safety plan (driving, firearms, stove, wandering), a care roadmap with cost projections and a Leqembi decision aid, and 90 days of dyad coaching.
why_now: FDA cleared Lumipulse pTau217 in May 2025 and a second primary-care blood test in Oct 2025. Leqembi Q1 sales rose 74% to $168M and it now has an at-home subcutaneous starting dose. Diagnosis is decentralizing while post-diagnosis coordination is not.
revenue_model: $1,500-3,500 fixed family fee, plus employer or LTC-insurer contracts. No referral payments from providers, to stay clear of anti-kickback issues.
non_obvious_insight: Earlier diagnosis is a legal-capacity clock, not just a medical event. The valuable window is the one when the patient can still sign, and every document signed in it prevents a $5-15k guardianship later.
first_30_days: Partner with two memory clinics and three elder-law firms, and deliver five pilot sprints at $1,500 each. Track documents executed while competent and family satisfaction.

title: Fraud-Proof Sourcing for the Dye-and-Whey Scramble
angle: Pairing 2: Food & agriculture x Cybersecurity/deepfake fraud/identity verification/scams
one_liner: A concierge service that authenticates certificates of analysis, brokers and supplier identities for supply-short ingredients such as natural colors and whey.
customer: Procurement and QA or regulatory teams at $50M-3B food, beverage and private-label manufacturers reformulating away from petroleum dyes (Walmart private label dye-free in Jan 2027, FDA target Dec 2027) or scrambling for whey.
problem: Natural colorant demand is projected to rise 400-500%, the US is 98% import-dependent for annatto, and reformulation costs $50K-500K per SKU over 12-24+ months. Whey concentrate is up 108% in two years and some suppliers are sold out through 2026. Shortages under deadline pressure bring new brokers, prepayment demands and adulteration risk. Generative AI makes certificates of analysis, lab letterheads and audit certificates trivial to forge, and QA teams verify by email.
solution: For each lot: a direct callback or API check with the issuing lab (signed lab-issued COAs where possible), document forensics (metadata, accreditation numbers versus registries), supplier identity and beneficial-owner checks, bank-account-name match to catch payment redirection, and importer-chain (FSVP) checks. Members contribute data to a pooled adulteration signature library (chromatography and spectral patterns) that becomes the moat.
why_now: Two hard deadlines (Walmart Jan 2027, FDA Dec 2027) and a whey shortage are forcing buyers to source from unfamiliar suppliers now. More than 70 alt-protein companies have folded or been acquired since September 2024, so distressed ingredient stock is moving through brokers. Forging documents with AI is now near-free.
revenue_model: $250-600 per verified lot on a concierge basis, then $2-6K a month subscriptions for monitoring and access to the member data pool, plus lab referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: In shortages the fraudster's edge is paperwork, not chemistry. Buyers under deadline pressure waive diligence. A KYC layer that never touches a molecule but is bonded to accredited labs can become the trust network, and the pooled fingerprint library gets more valuable with every member.
first_30_days: Reach 10 QA directors on LinkedIn. Offer the first 5 COA verifications free in exchange for lot data. Sign 2 accredited labs for callback verification. Publish a one-page 'natural color and whey counterfeits to watch' guide for lead generation. Convert 3 pilots at about $2,500 each.

title: Bone-First Strength Program for Women 45+
one_liner: A gym-delivered lifting and impact program for perimenopausal women, sold on DEXA-verified bone and muscle results.
customer: Women aged roughly 42-60 paying $79-149 per month, delivered through independent gyms, Pilates and strength studios and PT clinics that license the program.
problem: Women's fitness tech is fixated on cycle-syncing even though current evidence for cycle effects on performance is inconclusive, while midlife women (an 'invisible cohort' in sports science) face accelerating bone and muscle loss, worsened for those on GLP-1 drugs. Gyms sell toning and never measure the outcome that matters.
solution: A 24-week program of progressive heavy lifting, impact and balance work, with DEXA at baseline, 6 and 12 months via partner scan providers, simple bone-loading dose tracking with a hip or wrist sensor, coach training and a results dashboard studios use for retention. Positioned as wellness and performance with a physician advisor, not treatment.
why_now: Retail DEXA scans have dropped to roughly sub-$100, menopause is a mainstream topic, wearable makers are pouring money into women's health, perimenopause research is accelerating in 2026, and GLP-1 adoption has made bone and lean-mass loss a mass-market worry.
revenue_model: Member fees $79-149 per month; studio license $299-499 per month plus $30 per member; scan affiliate margin of $10-20 per scan.
non_obvious_insight: The moat is the outcome measurement: 'X percent of members held or gained bone density at 12 months' is a claim no gym can currently make, and the resulting dataset is valuable to clinicians and researchers. Cycle-syncing is a distraction from the larger midlife need.
first_30_days: Recruit 25 women aged 45-60 through two local strength gyms, book baseline DEXA scans with a retail or mobile provider, run a 12-week pilot with a physician advisor, and sign three studios to license the program off the interim results.

title: H.264 Royalty Sunset Desk for Streamers
one_liner: A country-by-country patent-expiry analysis and codec-delivery plan that cuts H.264/AVC streaming royalty exposure for mid-tier video services, paid partly on savings.
customer: Mid-size OTT and FAST channel operators, ed-tech, fitness, telehealth and cloud-gaming platforms and video-heavy social apps (well below the 100M-subscriber mega-tier). Buyer is the general counsel, CFO or head of video engineering.
problem: The Via LA AVC pool replaced its flat $100k streaming cap with tiered fees up to $4.5M a year, and added FAST and cloud-gaming categories, for a codec standardized in 2003. Press reports say US patent coverage runs out around 2028, so one analysis says paying $4.5M for about 18 months of coverage 'makes no economic sense'. Wikipedia and HN commenters put at least one US patent at 2030 and 'only 5 left' worldwide. Mid-tier operators can't tell what they actually owe.
solution: Ingest Via LA's public AVC patent attachment (re-issued 2026-09-28) plus national legal-status data, and build a live-patent map per country. Overlay each customer's audience by country and device. Deliver (a) a counsel-ready exposure memo to negotiate the right tier or challenge scope, (b) an engineering plan that serves AV1/VP9 in territories with live patents and H.264 where none remain, using a device-capability ladder, and (c) a countdown dashboard that also tracks HEVC and audio codecs. Work with a patent attorney partner so the memo is legal work product.
why_now: The new streaming fee schedule took effect in early 2026 (Tom's Hardware, Apr 3, 2026: fees raised 'from $100,000 up to $4.5 million'). The last MPEG-4 Part 2 patent expired 2026-07-19 and the last E-AC3 patents may have lapsed in 2026, so 'is it free yet?' is a live question. AV1 hardware decode is now common in 2023+ phones, TVs and PCs.
revenue_model: Fixed $15k-$40k audit and plan, plus about 20% of first-year royalty savings or avoided fees, plus $1k a month for the monitoring dashboard.
non_obvious_insight: Patent pools price by audience tier, not by how many patents are still alive, and patents are territorial and expire on different dates, so the expiry calendar itself is arbitrage. Evidence: Via LA's program page shows Tier 1 at $4.5M a year, small operators as low as $100k, new FAST and cloud-gaming tiers, and a patent attachment updated 2026-09-28 (https://www.via-la.com/licensing-2/avc-h-264/). The Wikipedia AVC entry notes many patents expired but at least one US patent runs to Nov 2030, and that Nokia sued HP and Amazon over H.264/H.265 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advanced_Video_Coding). The HN thread on the last Brazilian MPEG-4 patent expiring includes 'only 5 left' and a Siemens patent to 2030 (https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/items/49311814). Details of the expired Siemens BR patent: https://www.xda-developers.com/25-year-old-brazilian-video-patent-expired-legal-headache-linux/.
first_30_days: Days 1-14: scrape the Via LA patent list and build the per-country expiry table for AVC (a few weekends of work). Days 10-30: post the free 'H.264 patent death clock' as a public page, pitch 30 mid-size streaming and video-first SaaS companies from job boards and app-store data with a free exposure estimate, and offer a $7.5k pilot audit to the first 3 who reply. Retain a patent attorney on a flat fee to sign off on memo templates.

title: Practice-in-a-Box for Licensed Paraprofessionals
one_liner: Turn displaced paralegals into licensed legal paraprofessionals who can legally sell AI-leveraged flat-fee services directly to the public in states that now allow it.
customer: Displaced or at-risk paralegals and legal assistants, paying $149-299/month, who serve consumers with family law, landlord-tenant, and limited civil matters in states with limited-license programs (Arizona LP, Utah LPP, Oregon LP, Colorado LLP, Minnesota developing).
problem: AI has pushed the value of routine paralegal tasks toward zero inside law firms, while most low-income people's legal problems get little or no help. Several states created limited licenses for exactly this gap, but the licensed pool is tiny because the path (exams, supervised hours, malpractice insurance, trust accounting, client acquisition, tooling) is costly and lonely for a laid-off individual.
solution: A 'practice in a box' with exam and supervised-hours prep, a group malpractice policy, compliant trust accounting, standard intake and scope-check forms, an AI drafting stack with mandatory citation verification and human sign-off, and shared consumer marketing for flat-fee packages (for example, $900 uncontested divorce). It hands off cleanly to lawyers when a matter is out of scope. To respect fee-sharing rules, the company charges flat subscription fees, never a percentage of legal fees.
why_now: Entry-level paralegal roles are among the most cited casualties of 2026 AI layoffs. Colorado's LLP program launched in 2024, Arizona's has licensed since 2021, and Oregon approved its license in 2022. AI drafting makes flat-fee economics finally work for a solo practitioner.
revenue_model: $149-299/month practitioner subscription, exam-prep courses (about $600), group insurance commissions, and per-practitioner advertising placements where permitted.
non_obvious_insight: When AI drives the cost of doing legal work to near zero, the scarce asset is the license to sell it. Regulators created cheap licenses for access-to-justice reasons and they sit underused. Displaced paralegals are the natural supply. The moat is regulatory and operational, not technological.
first_30_days: Pick Arizona and Colorado. Recruit 15 laid-off paralegals through paralegal associations and LinkedIn. Sign a malpractice broker. Launch a $49 'is my matter in scope?' consumer screen as lead generation. Sell exam-prep and onboarding to the first 10 practitioners, about $2k in monthly recurring revenue plus course fees.

title: SNAP Rules Engine for Independent Grocers
one_liner: An API and POS plug-in that classifies every UPC against each state's changing SNAP soda and candy rules.
customer: Independent grocers and convenience stores in states with SNAP restrictions, and the POS and EBT vendors that serve them.
problem: 22 states have SNAP soda and candy restrictions in effect or pending, definitions differ by state, and a June 2026 ruling (Aragon v. Rollins) blocked waivers in five states, so rules keep flipping.
solution: A maintained UPC-level eligibility database by state and effective date, delivered as a POS plug-in and API with audit logs for SNAP authorization defense.
why_now: Patchwork state waivers and court reversals in 2026 mean retailers carry compliance liability without product-level data.
revenue_model: $30-60 per store per month, plus license fees from POS vendors.
non_obvious_insight: Court-driven rule flips make this a recurring data subscription rather than a one-time setup, and the liability sits with retailers who have no tooling.
first_30_days: Classify the top 5,000 UPCs for four states, pilot in 20 independent stores and one POS vendor, and set up a rule-change alert feed.

title: Verified-Human Capture for Robot Training Data
angle: Pairing 2: Logistics and physical automation x Trust and verification markets (lens: proving human and proving quality)
one_liner: A trusted-capture layer that proves robot training video was really filmed by a real human doing a real task on a real sensor, sold to data vendors and to the labs that buy from them.
customer: Robot-data collection networks (the long tail beneath XDOF and Mecka) and the humanoid makers and robot-foundation-model labs that buy their hours of first-person footage.
problem: Physical-world data is the humanoid bottleneck, and vendors pay gig workers to film themselves making coffee or fixing cars. Pay-per-effort markets get swamped by slop: cURL killed its bug bounty in Jan 2026 over AI-generated reports. AI video makes fake demos trivial. Workers can replay clips, script them or run multiple accounts, and buyers cannot QC hours at scale. One contaminated batch can poison a training run. Vendors grading their own data is the referee-grading-itself problem.
solution: A capture app and a certified head- or chest-mount kit that signs raw video, IMU and depth with device-bound keys in a C2PA-compatible manifest. Physics-consistency checks compare video-derived camera motion to the IMU trace, which generated video fails. Unique-worker checks without stored biometrics (on-device liveness, payout-account binding). Random human audit sampling and per-clip QA scores. A batch-level 'Certified Real' certificate buyers can verify.
why_now: Mecka is near a $500M valuation and XDOF hit about $50M annualized revenue within three months of leaving stealth. C2PA hit critical mass (TikTok joined in Jul 2026). EU AI Act Article 50 has applied since Aug 2, 2026. Biometric proof-of-personhood is being banned in places (Thailand, Kenya, Philippines), and verifier breaches (Persona, IDScan) push toward on-device proof.
revenue_model: $0.30-$1.50 per verified hour, paid by vendors who pass it through. $20/mo certified-kit rental per collector. Enterprise audits for large data buyers, $5k-$25k per batch program.
non_obvious_insight: In content, human-made is a nicety. In robot data, physically real and human-performed is the entire product, and synthetic data is a far cheaper competitor. A certificate showing which hours are real is what lets vendors keep a price premium, so vendors will pay for it. The verifier gets a toll on the fastest-growing data category without competing with anyone.
first_30_days: Ship an open-source signed-capture app and a physics-consistency checker. Offer 5 small data vendors a free audit of one sample batch and show them the share of clips that fail. Convert 2 to paid pilots at $2k-$5k/mo. Ship a 'Certified Real' batch stamp and a public verification page.

title: Contingency Recovery of Missed Rotable Repair Warranties
one_liner: A success-fee auditor that finds repaired aircraft components that failed inside the shop's warranty window, and turns them into filed claims and cash.
customer: Small and mid-size operators with their own stores and a thin materials team. That means regional airlines, Part 135 cargo feeders and air-ambulance fleets, and Part 145 shops that buy their own exchange units. They pay 20-25% of whatever cash or credit is recovered, and nothing up front.
problem: A repaired starter-generator, bleed valve, hydraulic pump or fuel control that fails 4 months after the shop visit is often covered by warranty. Almost nobody claims it. The tech pulling the unit at 3 AM is trying to make a 6 AM departure and never sees the warranty terms. The repair invoice sits in accounts payable as a PDF. The removal record sits in the maintenance system, and hours and cycles sit in a third place. One materials coordinator owns thousands of removals a year, with 30-90 day claim windows. Three other leaks go unclaimed as well: 'no fault found' evaluation fees on units that were still under warranty, unreturned exchange cores that turn into penalty charges, and repair turnaround-time guarantees that shops never credit because nobody compares PO date to receipt date.
solution: Ingest three exports: removals and installs, PO and repair invoices (PDFs read with an LLM extractor), and the negotiated warranty terms. Match by part number and serial number, including interchangeable P/Ns. Flag every in-warranty failure, late repair turn, disputable NFF fee and open core. Then draft the claim on each vendor's own template, track it to a paid credit, and re-run monthly. Add a 3 AM 'is this unit under warranty?' lookup for maintenance control, so the claim gets started at the moment of removal.
why_now: Airline cost pressure on regionals is high, and mechanic wages rose sharply in 2024-2026, so labor cost per removal is up. Materials teams are being cut while fleets stay old. LLM invoice and PDF extraction only became reliable and cheap enough in the last 18 months, and that is the missing link, because the money sits in unstructured AP documents that MRO software never reads.
revenue_model: Contingency fee of 20-25% of recovered cash and credits, with a 12-month tail on the audit. Later add a $2-5k per month SaaS tier for continuous monitoring, and sell benchmark data on shop warranty behavior to airline procurement teams.
non_obvious_insight: The leak is not in the maintenance system, it is in accounts payable. The tech who removes the part, the coordinator who could file the claim and the department that paid the invoice never share a screen. MRO software vendors will not fix it because warranty terms live in negotiated PDFs, not fields. Repair shops know most eligible claims are never filed, and they price that into their rates. A contingency auditor is the same playbook as freight-audit and telecom-audit firms, aimed at a niche nobody has covered.
first_30_days: Pitch 10 directors of maintenance and materials managers at small regionals, cargo feeders and helicopter EMS operators. Offer a free 12-month leakage audit, and ask them for the three exports. Build the matcher in Python plus an LLM invoice parser, and use a retired warranty or materials coordinator as a paid advisor for vendor quirks. Deliver a ranked claim list to the first 2-3 customers, file the claims yourself, and sign the success-fee agreement on the first credit memo. Publish the aggregate audit finding, such as the percentage of eligible failures that were never claimed, as the lead magnet.

title: Fresh-Fall Meteorite Alerts and Landowner Desk
angle: Pairing 2: Space economy x Weird/niche/overlooked markets (hobbies, collectibles, faith, subcultures)
one_liner: Turn satellite lightning-sensor fireball detections into strewn-field maps within an hour, then broker signed landowner access and sale terms for hunters and dealers who pay for a 24-hour head start.
customer: Serious meteorite hunters, dealers and collectors (a few thousand worldwide), with museums and labs as secondary buyers of fresh, uncontaminated samples.
problem: Value depends on freshness and documentation. A witnessed fall recovered before rain sells for many times the price per gram of desert finds, and in my recollection a Martian meteorite sold for about $5.3M at auction in 2025. Hunters race using scattered social posts and public bolide feeds that arrive late. Landowners own the meteorites in the US, so the hunter who lands the landowner's yes wins.
solution: A pipeline that ingests public geostationary lightning-mapper fireball detections, weather-radar falling-debris signatures and upper-air winds to publish a dark-flight strewn ellipse in minutes. It overlays parcel data and gives the desk a landowner script, a one-page finder-landowner split contract, and a provenance dossier (time, coordinates, radar and satellite evidence) that raises sale price. Paid subscribers get the alert first.
why_now: GOES-19 became the operational eastern US geostationary satellite in 2025, with lightning imagers now covering the Americas and, as I understand it, Europe and East Asia. Open radar data is on the cloud, and the collectibles market is at extremes (a $16.5M single card in Feb 2026). LLM pipelines make a two-person alerting desk feasible.
revenue_model: $15 per month for hunter alerts, a $49 event pass for high-value falls, and 10% of sale value on brokered recoveries. Dealers pay about $300 per month for a priority feed and the landowner contract kit.
non_obvious_insight: Detection is free public data. The scarce input is speed to a signed landowner agreement before rain and rivals arrive. The business is a contracts-and-logistics desk that happens to run on satellite data, and the provenance dossier is the price multiplier.
first_30_days: Script the public fireball feeds and backtest on 2021-2025 falls. Open a Discord with 200 hunters and 5 dealers, and pre-sell 30 annual passes at $99. Offer to run the next credible fall end to end using the contract template, taking a percentage only if material is recovered.

title: Storm-Chaser Livestreams as Claims Evidence
angle: Pairing 1: Climate adaptation x Gaming/entertainment/live experiences/fandoms
one_liner: License the timestamped, geotagged archives of storm-chaser channels as address-level date-of-loss evidence for hail, wind and flood claims.
customer: Public adjusters, policyholder attorneys and roofing-claim desks in hail states (Colorado, Texas, Nebraska, Minnesota) first. Parametric hail and wind MGAs and appraisal umpires second.
problem: Hail claims turn on whether hail of a given size hit an address on a given date. Radar estimates are error-prone at swath edges, and spotter reports are sparse. Hail drives 26-54% of Colorado premiums (secondary source). Colorado's HB25-1182 (in force since July 2026) and California's AB 75 give owners disclosure and appeal rights, but the evidence burden stays on them ('owners still have to prove their case'). Meanwhile storm chasers stream thousands of hours with GPS, timestamps and hailstones held next to coins, and that ground truth sits unmonetized on YouTube.
solution: Sign revenue-share licenses with chaser channels. Index their archives by time, location and hail size, using computer vision on reference objects, and pair each clip with radar. Sell a 'Date-of-Loss Dossier' per address: nearest verified clips, size estimate, uncertainty and chain of custody. Distribute a printed reference 'hail card' standard to chasers. Add a 'go verify' request queue where adjusters or parametric carriers post bounties on active storms and fans can top them up by tipping.
why_now: Storm-chase livestreaming is now a fan-funded media business with huge live audiences. New state laws create disputes that need evidence. Parametric MGAs need data that cuts basis risk. The 2025-26 hail seasons are still inside claim windows, and the spring 2027 season is six months away, so the archive-first version can sell now.
revenue_model: $39-149 per dossier from public adjusters and roofers, $2-5K a month API access for MGAs and claims shops, and 40-50% revenue share to creators.
non_obvious_insight: The densest hail sensor network in America is a fandom already paid for by fans. Insurers' problem is not data volume but admissible, attributable data, and chasers go exactly to the worst cell. Ground truth is a by-product of entertainment, so the sensor cost is already covered.
first_30_days: Approach 15 mid-size chaser channels (10K-300K subscribers) with a rev-share license for their 2024-26 archives. Index 200 hail events. Sell the first 50 dossiers to 5 Colorado and Texas public adjusters and roofing claim reps for open claims. Draft the reference-card standard for the spring 2027 season.

title: Pre-Dawn Childcare Pods for Construction Crews
angle: Pairing 2: Construction/housing/skilled-trades/home services x Parenting/childcare deserts/Gen Alpha/kids and AI-screens
one_liner: Contractors buy reserved 5:00am-4:00pm childcare slots near job sites from licensed home providers, so crews can start at 6am without losing parents.
customer: General contractors and specialty subs (electrical, framing, concrete), especially on data-center and big subdivision projects, plus local homebuilder associations and apprenticeship funds. The 45F credit lets them recover 40-50% of the cost.
problem: Crews start at 5:30-7am and often work 10-12 hour days, but licensed care opens at 6:30-7am. ICE enforcement, retirements and data-center overtime are already draining the workforce, and construction is only about 4% women. Providers cannot staff 5am hours without guaranteed revenue. Childcare workers earn about $33K, so nobody can afford premium-hour pay.
solution: Contract with licensed family providers and small centers near job sites and staging areas to run early-hours pods with reserved capacity on a monthly retainer. Cap care at a safe number of hours (about 10) and design for early-arrival sleep. The platform handles enrollment, insurance, shift scheduling, drop-off logistics and 45F paperwork. For megasites with thousands of workers, add factory-built child-care modules on site.
why_now: The 45F credit rose to 40% (50% for small businesses) from 2026 and reportedly allows third-party and pooled arrangements, so a group of subs can share one program. ABC says construction must add 349K workers in 2026, immigrant workers are over 25% of the workforce and are being pulled off sites, and data centers are absorbing about a third of the shortage. Retention is the acute buyer pain.
revenue_model: $350-600 per reserved slot per month paid by contractors, 12-15% platform fee on top of provider pay, and tax-credit advisory fees.
non_obvious_insight: The people who cannot use standard 7-6 childcare are the only buyers who will pay a premium, and construction employers already pay per-diems, housing and overtime to keep skilled hands. Replacing one journeyman costs thousands, so a few hundred dollars a month for a reliable slot is cheap. A retainer is what unlocks provider supply for the early hours.
first_30_days: Choose one metro with a data-center or subdivision surge. Interview 10 subs' HR or safety directors and survey crews on childcare needs. Sign two family providers willing to open at 5am for guaranteed pay. Sell a pilot of 10 reserved slots to one mid-size electrical or framing contractor, then get a CPA to sign off on the 45F treatment.

title: Rural Vet Call Logs as Outbreak Early Warning
one_liner: Producers call the vet before they call the state. Anonymized weekly counts of abortions, maggot wounds, sudden deaths and respiratory clusters are a leading indicator that traders, insurers and packers will pay for.
customer: Buyers: cattle and feeder analytics desks, market advisory and commodity funds, packer and feedlot risk managers, livestock and dairy insurers or reinsurers, animal health company territory teams, and state animal health boards (contracts or grants). Suppliers are participating rural vets, who get free early regional alerts and a small revenue share.
problem: Official disease data lags by weeks because it waits on lab confirmation, and ranchers hesitate to report to the state because a quarantine costs them money. Screwworm was confirmed in a Texas calf in June 2026 after roughly 60 years without a US case, and H5N1 in dairy cattle was spreading for months before detection in 2024. Cattle futures at record prices with a 70-year low herd move violently on rumor, and nobody has a systematic ground-level feed.
solution: A 30-second end-of-week SMS or one-tap tally where each vet reports counts by syndrome (abortion clusters, navel or wound maggots, sudden deaths, neurological, respiratory, milk drops) and ZIP3 or county. Counts are aggregated with k-anonymity (no client identity, minimum practice thresholds) and compared to seasonal baselines. Outputs are a weekly 'Rural Vet Pulse' regional index, push alerts when a region deviates, and an API for institutional subscribers. Vets get the regional alerts free, which is the give-to-get hook.
why_now: New World screwworm has been confirmed in Texas and New Mexico since June 2026, with the first infested horse reported in September 2026, and movement restrictions plus sterile-fly shortages make the outbreak's trajectory the biggest driver of cattle risk. H5N1 in dairy is ongoing, federal animal health staffing is stretched, and academic syndromic surveillance systems exist in Europe (Netherlands, France, Great Britain) but I found no commercial equivalent built from US rural vet practices.
revenue_model: $2-10K per month per institutional data subscriber (analytics desks, insurers, packers), enterprise API tiers, sponsored regional alerts from animal health companies, state or regional government pilots, and a $100-300 per month revenue share to each contributing practice.
non_obvious_insight: Ranchers under-report to the state because reporting costs them money, but they do not hide problems from their vet because they need the vet's drugs and help. The vet's phone is the earliest sensor in the system, and vets cannot share client data but can share counts. Contrarian point: the absence of calls is also a signal, because call volume drops when producers hide problems during a quarantine.
first_30_days: Recruit 25 large-animal practices in Texas, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Kansas and Nebraska through state VMA lists and large-animal vet Facebook groups. Build the weekly tally as a plain SMS survey, with no software integration. Publish a free regional weekly newsletter to the vets as the hook. Backtest screwworm lead time against USDA confirmation dates and pitch 3 market-advisory or cattle analytics shops for a $1-2K per month paid pilot.
